title: Detect Squares
statement: Build a structure that stores points on a plane. add(point) stores one point, and the same point may be added many times. count(point) says how many ways there are to pick three stored points that, together with the query point, form an axis-aligned square with area above zero. Stored copies count separately.

example.caption: Stored: (1,3), (4,0), (1,0). The query (4,3) is the fourth corner of the square with side 3, so count is 1.

input.label: stored points (x across, y up). ? = the query

idea.sentence: Keep a count of copies per point. To answer a query, treat each stored point on the diagonal as the opposite corner, then look up the other two corners and multiply their copy counts.

jargon.plain: A square whose sides are parallel to the x and y axes, so no tilted squares.
A stored point that is the same distance from the query across (x) as up (y), and not zero. It can be the corner opposite the query.
You write a class with methods. Tests call a list of operations and check each result.

watch.inputHint: Two arguments: operation names, then their arguments. e.g. ["DetectSquares","add","count"], [[],[1,3],[4,3]]. Keep coordinates between 0 and 7 to see the grid.

vars.meaning: number of points added so far (repeats counted)

compare.bruteLabel: Try every triple of stored points
compare.optimalLabel: Look at each stored point once, two map lookups

rows.name: Try every triple
rows.note: Check whether each three stored points and the query form a square. Far too slow.

rows.name: Diagonal + count map
rows.note: One pass over the stored points. Each diagonal one costs two O(1) lookups.

fast.takeaway: The query point and its diagonal opposite already decide the whole square: the other two corners are forced. So three nested loops collapse into one.

stages.title: Store the point
stages.note: add: bump the copy count in the map and keep the point in a list for later scans.

stages.title: Find a diagonal point
stages.note: count: for every stored point, skip it unless it is equally far across and up from the query, and not zero away.

stages.title: Look up the other corners
stages.note: The other two corners are fixed by the query and the diagonal point. Multiply their copy counts and add to the total.

stages.title: Return the total
stages.note: After all stored points are tried, the sum is the answer.

edges.title: Empty structure
edges.why: The list is empty, so the loop does nothing and the total stays 0.

edges.title: Query equals a stored point
edges.why: A zero-size square has no area. The check px === qx (or distance 0) removes it.

edges.title: Rectangle, not a square
edges.why: The distance across is 3 but up is 2, so the diagonal test fails. A rectangle is not a square.

edges.title: Duplicates multiply
edges.why: Each copy of the diagonal point makes a different square, so the total multiplies the copy counts.

gotchas.text: A Map with an array key, like map.set([x, y], 1), never finds the key again, because two arrays with the same numbers are different objects. Use a string key such as `${x},${y}`.

Loop over the list of added points (repeats included), not over the map keys, and multiply only the two other corners. Then duplicates of the diagonal point are counted once each, with no extra factor.
An array like [2]int is comparable, so it works directly as a map key: map[[2]int]int. A slice []int is not allowed as a key. Keep the x, y pair in a [2]int.

Reading a missing map key returns 0 for an int map, so d.copies[p] needs no ok check and missing corners multiply to 0 on their own. The only risk is using d.copies[p]++ before the map was made with make or a literal.
Test equal distance with absolute values: |px - qx| == |py - qy|. A signed difference misses squares to the left and below the query.

recap.key: Store copies per point. For count, each stored diagonal point fixes the other two corners. Multiply their counts.
recap.complexity: add O(1). count O(n) over stored points. Space O(n).
moves: add: copies[point]++ and push to list
count: for each stored point, skip unless |dx| == |dy| and dx != 0
Multiply copies of the two other corners
